title: Lunda: alliances and connections
question: How does power extend through alliances and networks?
standfirst: Lunda history intersects with Luba and Chokwe histories without merging into them. Origin traditions, relations between courts and exchanges require distinct readings.

figures.claim: Bortolot places Mwaant Yaav Naweej’s connections to the Atlantic coast around this period.
figures.provenance: An approximate date in a historical synthesis.

chapters.title: Origins and legitimacy
chapters.question: What does an origin tradition tell us?
chapters.standfirst: A political genealogy is not a calendar.

body.text: Traditions reported by Bortolot connect Chibinda Ilunga, a hunter from the Luba world, to a Lunda marriage alliance. He presents an origin tradition, not a dated founding document.
This Chokwe sculpture evokes Chibinda Ilunga without providing a verifiable portrait.

readings.label: A memory of power
readings.body: The sanza accompanies historical recitations and praise songs.

readings.label: Distinct societies
readings.body: A shared reference does not merge Chokwe and Lunda societies.

illustration.alt: Standing figure holding a sanza, with a broad carved headdress.
illustration.caption: Chokwe mwanangana playing a sanza, before 1869. An evocation of Chibinda Ilunga.

chapters.title: Expansion and reorganisation
chapters.question: Should we imagine a state with fixed borders?
chapters.standfirst: Routes and relationships change alongside centres of power.

body.text: The Met chronology describes the emergence of Kazembe in the eighteenth century in present-day north-eastern Zambia. This eastern extension forms another political centre, connected to exchanges between the east coast and the interior.
Macola also uses Commonwealth for independent but interconnected states. This clarifies what empire can conceal: multiple centres and political autonomy.

readings.label: Following networks
readings.body: Political and trading connections link several territories. They do not imply identical administration everywhere.

readings.label: Exchange involves violence
readings.body: The entry also recalls regional trade in ivory and enslaved people.

gaps.reason: The dates of origin traditions remain debated. Present-day countries locate places; they do not define an empire that stayed unchanged through the centuries.
